description: AV1's superblock partition tree decomposed. A 128x128 (or 64x64) superblock is recursively split via a 10-way decision tree until each leaf block reaches its terminal size (typically 4x4 to 64x64). The 10 partition types extend the quadtree-only model of VP9/HEVC with binary, ternary, and 4-way splits — matching real image structure more naturally.

sub_mechanisms.name: split_NONE
sub_mechanisms.definition: Terminal: this block is not split further; it becomes a leaf coding unit.
sub_mechanisms.why: Encoder picks this when further splitting wouldn't help R-D cost. The 'no further split' decision is a partition type itself, costing 1 bit but identifying that this block is the final analysis unit.

sub_mechanisms.name: split_SPLIT
sub_mechanisms.definition: Quadtree split into 4 equal sub-blocks (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right). Each can be further partitioned.
sub_mechanisms.why: The classical quadtree split, inherited from HEVC. Optimal for symmetric content patterns; the 'safe choice' that's always available.

sub_mechanisms.name: split_HORZ
sub_mechanisms.definition: Binary horizontal split into top half + bottom half (each block_size/2 in height).
sub_mechanisms.why: Matches vertically-oriented content boundaries (horizontal lines, lying objects, text rows). 1 split decision instead of needing the full quadtree to express it; saves signalling bits.

sub_mechanisms.name: split_VERT
sub_mechanisms.definition: Binary vertical split into left half + right half (each block_size/2 in width).
sub_mechanisms.why: Matches horizontally-oriented content boundaries (vertical lines, standing objects, columns). Symmetric counterpart to HORZ; together they cover the rectangular-split cases that quadtree can't directly express.

sub_mechanisms.name: split_HORZ_A
sub_mechanisms.definition: T-shaped split: a horizontal split at the top creates two side-by-side sub-blocks (each block_size/4 height), with the bottom half a single block.
sub_mechanisms.why: Matches L-shaped content (e.g., a frame border + main image area). The split's irregularity captures L-shaped object boundaries with one decision instead of the multiple quadtree splits otherwise needed.

sub_mechanisms.name: split_HORZ_B
sub_mechanisms.definition: Mirror of HORZ_A: the top half is a single block, the bottom is split into two side-by-side blocks.
sub_mechanisms.why: Same insight as HORZ_A, mirrored. Covers the inverted L-shape; together with HORZ_A handles all four T-shape orientations sharing a horizontal axis of symmetry.

sub_mechanisms.name: split_VERT_A
sub_mechanisms.definition: T-shape with axis of symmetry on the vertical: left vertical split into two stacked sub-blocks, right half a single block.
sub_mechanisms.why: Same insight as HORZ_A but for vertically-oriented L-shapes. Each direction's pair (HORZ_A/B, VERT_A/B) is together a natural set for any L-shape orientation.

sub_mechanisms.name: split_VERT_B
sub_mechanisms.definition: Mirror of VERT_A: left a single block, right split into two stacked sub-blocks.
sub_mechanisms.why: Completes the T-shape family. With HORZ_A/B + VERT_A/B + SPLIT, AV1 can describe all the natural L-shape configurations that arise at object boundaries.

sub_mechanisms.name: split_HORZ_4
sub_mechanisms.definition: 4-way horizontal split into 4 horizontal strips, each block_size/4 in height (full width).
sub_mechanisms.why: Matches multiple horizontal text rows or thin horizontal lines (e.g., bookcase shelves, hairline edges). One 4-way split instead of 3 binary splits saves ~2 bits of signalling.

sub_mechanisms.name: split_VERT_4
sub_mechanisms.definition: 4-way vertical split into 4 vertical strips, each block_size/4 in width (full height).
sub_mechanisms.why: Symmetric counterpart to HORZ_4. Together they handle long-strip content patterns that quadtree would need 3 splits + extra coding to express.

sub_mechanisms.name: partition_signalling_context
sub_mechanisms.definition: The chosen partition type is signalled per node via a CDF context derived from the node's block size + the partition types of spatial neighbours.
sub_mechanisms.why: Partition statistics correlate spatially (a frame with lots of HORZ_4 in one region tends to have it nearby). CDF context exploits this via the multi-symbol arithmetic coder's CDF tables — partition signalling drops to <1 bit per node on average.

sub_mechanisms.name: partition_size_constraints
sub_mechanisms.definition: Not every partition type is legal at every size. E.g., HORZ_4 is illegal at 8x8 (would give 8x2 blocks below the 4x4 minimum). The decoder enforces these via implicit context.
sub_mechanisms.why: Block-size constraints prevent partitions that would violate the 4x4 minimum or produce non-rectangular shapes. The decoder doesn't need to be told which partitions are legal — it derives them from the current block size, saving signalling bits.

derivation_rules.name: asymmetric_splits_match_object_boundaries
if: object boundaries in real images are rarely quadtree-symmetric
then: T-shape (HORZ_A/B, VERT_A/B) partitions cheaply capture them
derivation_rules.why: Quadtree alone forces splits to align on the same axis at every depth. Real boundaries don't. T-shape partitions express L-shapes in one decision; without them, the encoder needs 2-3 quadtree levels and pays for each unnecessary split.

derivation_rules.name: ternary_4way_splits_match_strip_content
if: content contains long thin horizontal or vertical strips (text rows, thin objects)
then: HORZ_4 or VERT_4 partitions save ~2 bits per region vs binary splits
derivation_rules.why: Each binary split costs ~1 bit. 4 strips in 3 binary splits = 3 bits; in one 4-way split = 1 bit. Multiplied across the many strip regions in typical content, the saving is substantial.

derivation_rules.name: partition_cdf_context_amortises_signalling
then: CDF-based signalling drops per-node bit cost below 1
derivation_rules.why: Multi-symbol arithmetic coder with CDF context derives per-node probability from neighbours' choices. In coherent regions (frame border, large flat area), partition choices are predictable; the average cost drops well below the entropy of a uniform distribution.

derivation_rules.name: partition_legality_derived_not_signalled
if: the decoder knows the current block size
then: it can derive which partitions are legal without signalling
derivation_rules.why: Many partitions are illegal at small sizes (would create sub-4x4 blocks). The decoder enforces these via context-derived constraints. Saves signalling bits by not transmitting choices that couldn't be made.
